claim: /end runs alone, in its own turn, after the session's substantive close is complete; it is never invoked inline in a turn that also does close work. The Stop hook's render only reaches the previous completed turn, so /end run in a later turn reads a render that already includes the close turn and the finalized thread document's embedded transcript body contains it; the only omitted turn is the /end invocation turn itself, which carries no decision content and needs no disclosure. /end invoked inline emits a warning that the current turn will not be captured in the finalized body. Same-turn successive finalization (a /final running the close and the finalize in one turn) does not satisfy this and is rejected: a turn boundary is a separate exchange, not a second skill call.

evidence.detail: Operator decision in the end-skill round-trip session (2026-07-03): /end must always be called alone and never run inline, because the Stop hook render lags to the previous completed turn, so an inline /end omits the close turn from the finalized body (the cb:b518 tail-gap landing on the curated artifact). Deliberated in beliefs/nursery/end-skill-redesign.md; the render-pointer alternative was rejected on a duplication argument in favor of keeping the self-contained embedded body and running /end in a later turn.
